question: In which year was the World Wide Web invented?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1989**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Wide Web (WWW) was invented by **Tim Berners-Lee** in 1989.
 
• Tim Berners-Lee was a computer scientist working at **CERN** (the European Organization for Nuclear Research) when he invented the World Wide Web.
 
• The primary goal of the World Wide Web was to enable researchers to share data and information easily across the globe.
 
• The first website, created by Tim Berners-Lee, provided information about the World Wide Web project and was launched on **August 6, 1991**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Wide Web (WWW)**

 
 
• The World Wide Web, commonly known as the web, is a system of interlinked hypertext documents that are accessed via the internet.
 
• Users can access web pages that contain text, images, videos, and other multimedia, and navigate between them using hyperlinks.
 
• The web operates on the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), which defines how messages are formatted and transmitted, and how web servers and browsers should respond to various commands.
 
• Tim Berners-Lee also developed the first web browser, called WorldWideWeb (later renamed Nexus), and the first web server, known as CERN httpd.
 
 
 
• **Tim Berners-Lee**
 
 
• Sir Timothy John Berners-Lee, an English engineer and computer scientist, is best known for inventing the World Wide Web.
 
• He is also the director of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), which oversees the development of web standards to ensure the long-term growth of the web.
 
• In 2004, he was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II for his pioneering work on the World Wide Web.
 
• Berners-Lee continues to advocate for an open and accessible internet for everyone.
 
 
 
• **CERN**
 
 
• The European Organization for Nuclear Research, known as CERN, is one of the world's largest and most respected centers for scientific research in particle physics.
 
• Located on the border between France and Switzerland, CERN is home to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the world's largest and most powerful particle accelerator.
 
• CERN's primary mission is to explore the fundamental structure of the universe by studying the smallest particles that make up matter.
 
 
 
• **Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)**
 
 
• HTTP is the foundation of data communication for the World Wide Web.
 
• It is an application layer protocol used for transmitting hypermedia documents, such as HTML.
 
• HTTP defines how messages are formatted and transmitted, and how web servers and browsers should respond to various commands.
 
• It was developed by Tim Berners-Lee and his team at CERN as part of the World Wide Web project.
